speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are having trouble conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity. To help me understand your condition, have you noticed any specific pain location, such as deep pelvic pain or pain at the entrance?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor dysfunction with concurrent infertility evaluation. The patient reports deep pelvic pain and muscle tension during penetration, and her partner has erectile difficulties. Given the 15 months of trying to conceive, I will order a Pelvic_Floor_Assessment and Semen_Analysis to evaluate for vaginismus, endometriosis, or male-factor infertility.
